BELRISE: Manufacturing-led growth and expanding assembly, electronics and aerospace wins underpin unchanged guidance
Belrise Industries shares jump 11% as Q2 profit rises 25% YoY; revenue grows 17%
Belrise Industries shares jump 11% as Q2 profit rises 25% YoY; revenue grows 17%
items.summary: Belrise Industries shares rallied 10.50% to Rs 237.78 during Monday’s trading session after the company reported 25% year-on-year (YoY) growth in profit after tax (PAT) and a 17% increase in revenue from operations for the September quarter (Q2 FY27).Belrise Industries Limited (BIL), an integrated automotive component manufacturer, announced its financial results for Q2 FY27 and the first half of FY27, reporting growth in both revenue and profitability.The company's revenue from operations increased 17% YoY to Rs 2,746 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,353 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Profit after tax (PAT) rose 25% to Rs 166 crore from Rs 133 crore in Q2 FY26.Belrise Industries Q2 FY27 business highlightsThe company's manufacturing revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs 23,441 million in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 18,601 million in the year-ago quarter. Manufacturing EBITDA increased 19% to Rs 3,170 million from Rs 2,663 million in Q2 FY26. Manufacturing EBITDA margin stood at 13.5% during the quarter. Additionally, 71% of the company's manufacturing revenue came from powertrain-neutral products.Belrise Industries H1 FY27 performanceFor the first half of FY27, manufacturing revenue increased 23% YoY to Rs 45,420 million, compared with Rs 36,923 million in H1 FY26. Manufacturing EBITDA rose 15% to Rs 5,963 million from Rs 5,199 million in the corresponding period last year. The manufacturing EBITDA margin stood at 13.1%, while powertrain-neutral products accounted for 71% of manufacturing revenue.Belrise Industries secures new ordersDuring the quarter, Belrise Industries secured several new orders across its commercial vehicle and two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses. The company won a programme from a leading Indian commercial vehicle manufacturer to supply complete chassis frame assemblies across its heavy commercial vehicle (HCV) platforms. The supplies will be made from a new facility in Dharwad, with production expected to ramp up from Q1 FY28.The programme is expected to add Rs 60,000–1 lakh in content per vehicle, with peak annual revenue potential of Rs 1,500–2,000 million.Belrise also entered complete three-wheeler body manufacturing after being selected as the second source for complete body and chassis assemblies for a high-selling model of a leading Indian two-wheeler and three-wheeler manufacturer. The order represents incremental content of approximately Rs 9,000 per vehicle.Production from its new facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is expected to ramp up from Q1 FY28, with peak annual revenue potential of Rs 1,000–1,200 million.In its suspension business, the company onboarded its sixth original equipment manufacturer (OEM) customer, a leading premium two-wheeler manufacturer in South India. Supplies commenced in Q3 FY27. It also secured additional orders from a growing two-wheeler and three-wheeler OEM, with production expected to begin in Q4 FY27.What management saidCommenting on the company's Q2 and H1 FY27 performance, Shrikant Badve, Managing Director of Belrise Industries, said the quarter was marked by strong execution and a healthy demand environment. He highlighted that manufacturing revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs 23,441 million, while adjusted PAT increased 25% to Rs 1,663 million.Also read: Tata Motors PV shares crack 9% as Motilal Oswal cuts earnings estimates, stays bearish after Q2 resultsThe company also secured its maiden Letter of Intent (LoI) for the supply of CNC fixtures to an ecosystem partner of one of the largest American smartphone companies.According to Badve, India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem is poised to become one of the country's largest and most cost-competitive manufacturing segments. The new order will provide Belrise with an opportunity to demonstrate its precision engineering capabilities developed over the years.Share PriceBelrise Industries shares have rallied 45% over the past one year. The stock is currently trading at a market capitalisation of Rs 21,567 crore. items.summary:
State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has taken over operations and control of the disputed Cambay offshore block from Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd following a Delhi High Court ruling, according to regulatory filings by the two companies.
Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd has recognised an impairment charge of about Rs 379 crore against assets and receivables linked to the block.
The takeover of the CB-OS-02 block took effect on July 22, 2026, after the High Court's single-judge bench dismissed Vedanta's challenge to the government's decision not to extend the production-sharing contract, ONGC said in its quarterly filing.
The block was operated by Vedanta, which held a 40 per cent participating interest; ONGC held 50 per cent, and Invenire Petrodyne Ltd had the remaining 10 per cent.
The government, through a September 19, 2025, letter, declined to extend the contract and directed the operator to hand over the block to ONGC.
Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court

Edelweiss Financial Services Q2 FY27 results: Profit rises 18% to ₹207 cr
items.summary:
Edelweiss Financial Services on Friday reported an 18 per cent growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 207 crore for the second quarter ended September.
The company had earned a profit of Rs 175 crore in the corresponding quarter of the preceding fiscal.
Total income increased to Rs 2,602 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 1,900 crore in the year-ago period, Edelweiss Financial Services said in a regulatory filing.
Interest income rose to Rs 720 crore from Rs 687 crore in the same quarter a year ago.
During the quarter, total expenses also rose to Rs 2,393 crore from Rs 1,946 crore in the same period a year ago.
The company completed the Rs 1,200-crore IPO of its subsidiary Edelweiss Alternatives last month.
Earlier this year, global investment management firm Carlyle became a strategic majority investor in another subsidiary of the company, Nido Home Finance, with an investment of Rs 2,000 crore.
